declared: 2026-09-19, frozen before any simulation of this construction ran
question: Can visitation and mean-return information remain unchanged while the allocation appropriate for CVaR changes substantially, and does a learned pilot capture the available gain after paying for itself?

construction.type: one-step fixed stochastic policy, uniform over G independently queryable action kernels; a transparent special case of the paper's model (no multi-step reuse; CliffWalking supplies the sequential test)
construction.mixing: Pbar = [A + (G-1)B]/G; kernel g gets (1-t)*Pbar + t*endpoint_g, where the separated endpoint gives kernel 0 law A and kernels 1..9 law B
construction.analytical_checks: at every t: visitation, all kernel means and variances, and the root return law are unchanged; uniform/oracle leading-variance ratios approximately 1, 1.300, 10 at t = 0, .5, 1; separated endpoint: quantile 1/3, CVaR .3, margin .09; these must be reproduced by the engine before simulation results are read

grid: exact attainable outcome values (union over kernels) - representation error zero
rollout_accounting: one rollout = one environment sample (the known action policy is sampled for free); rollout visits are charged per drawn kernel outcome at matched total sampling cost
support_rule: learned laws use the full declared support of all outcome values; no method is told which kernel is exceptional
outputs: pilot underallocation of the influential kernel
uncertainty on primary method differences (paired where streams shared)
realized allocation or variance ratios for failure accounting
primary_comparison: t in {0, .5, 1} at all declared budgets; the t=0 equal-influence control must remain visible in every display
completion_criterion: a short separation proposition with a checked proof, one compact learning figure including the t=0 control, and a clear account of budgets where learning helps or hurts
